targets.authors: Wiseheart, M., Viswanathan, M., & Bialystok, E.
targets.title: Flexibility in task switching by monolinguals and bilinguals
targets.evidence_quote: This study aimed to closely replicate Wiseheart et al. ( Bilingualism: Language and Cognition , 19(1), 141–146, 2016) by investigating the transferability of language-switching skills to nonlinguistic task switching.
targets.outcome_quote: This replication study supported previous findings indicating that some bilingual individuals possess advantages in terms of cognitive flexibility in task switching.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The conclusion gives an overall supportive verdict. The original GSC advantage and absence of a significant LSC advantage were reproduced using the original analyses. Additional Bayesian LSC analyses do not constitute failure of an originally positive LSC effect, since the original reported none.

reasoning: New bilingual and monolingual sample explicitly closely replicates Wiseheart et al. Other task-switching papers are background rather than additional targets.
